title: Ulyana and the Tide
premise: Beatrix Underhill saved her family's failing vineyard by taking a job she never wanted: corporate fixer for the shipping conglomerate that once tried to buy her land. When a letter lost in the mail for eleven years resurfaces — written by her first love, Ulyana, on the night Beatrix left their island town without a word — it forces both women to confront the lie Beatrix told to survive. As Beatrix's employer closes in on the ferry route that is Ulyana's livelihood, the two must decide whether love can survive what power has made of them. In the end, Beatrix walks away from the career that saved everything, boards the last ferry of the season, and chooses Ulyana and a smaller, truer life.
about_author: Mirabel Okafor is a former maritime journalist who spent a decade covering coastal economies before turning to fiction. She writes from a converted boathouse, where the tide dictates her working hours.

chapters.title: The Letter in the Wall
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. During renovations at the vineyard, a contractor finds a water-stained letter postmarked eleven years ago, addressed to Beatrix from Ulyana. She recognizes the handwriting instantly and hides it unopened in her desk drawer. Emotional beat: dread wrapped in longing; the past knocking at a door she bricked over.

chapters.title: Small Safe Steps
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. A day in her carefully ordered life: harvest logistics, a board call with Meridian Shipping, dinner alone. She almost opens the letter twice. Flashback fragments hint at the night she left the island. Emotional beat: the suffocating comfort of control.

chapters.title: What the Tide Kept
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. On Harrow Island, Ulyana runs the ferry service her father built, now barely solvent. She learns Meridian is surveying the route for privatization. She doesn't know Beatrix works for Meridian. Emotional beat: stubborn pride guarding a crumbling inheritance.

chapters.title: Eleven Years of Silence
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. She finally reads the letter: Ulyana wrote that she'd wait at the dock until midnight, that she'd chosen Beatrix over leaving. Beatrix never came — because of a phone call, a threat, a choice made in panic. Emotional beat: grief arriving eleven years late.

chapters.title: The Assignment
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Her boss assigns her to lead the Harrow Island acquisition personally — the ferry route, the docks, the town's only artery. She accepts before she can refuse. Emotional beat: the trap closing with a handshake.

chapters.title: Crossing Over
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. The ferry carries a Meridian delegation, and Ulyana sees Beatrix step off the gangway. Eleven years collapse into one look across the deck. Neither speaks. Emotional beat: shock sharpening into fury.

chapters.title: Terms of Engagement
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Forced into a negotiation neither wants, they conduct business with surgical politeness while old wounds bleed underneath. Ulyana refuses Meridian's first offer flatly. Emotional beat: two people weaponizing composure.

chapters.title: The Vineyard at Night
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Ulyana appears at the vineyard after dark, not to negotiate but to demand the truth about why Beatrix vanished. Beatrix gives her half of it. They argue in the rows of vines until the anger breaks into something else. Emotional beat: honesty as a dangerous door opening.

chapters.title: What Power Buys
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Back at headquarters, Beatrix discovers Meridian plans to gut the ferry service and replace it with a private marina — the town was never the point, just the waterfront. She sits on the information. Emotional beat: complicity settling like sediment.

chapters.title: Salt and Memory
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Ulyana takes Beatrix out on the evening run, showing her the island the way locals see it. Old intimacy resurfaces in small gestures — steering close, shared silence. Emotional beat: tenderness relearning its language.

chapters.title: The Second Offer
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Meridian sweetens the deal with numbers that could save Ulyana's drowning business — if she abandons the route. Ulyana wavers, hating herself for it. Beatrix realizes she wants Ulyana to refuse for reasons beyond duty. Emotional beat: temptation wearing a fair face.

chapters.title: Confession at Low Tide
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. On the mudflats at low tide, Beatrix tells Ulyana the whole truth: the threat came from Ulyana's own father, who blackmailed Beatrix into leaving to protect his daughter's future. Ulyana reels. Emotional beat: the past revealed as more complicated than betrayal.

chapters.title: Fathers and Debts
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Ulyana confronts her dying father in the care home; he neither confirms nor denies, but gives her a box of letters he intercepted — including others Beatrix sent. Emotional beat: rage and pity tangled together.

chapters.title: Everything I Built
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Beatrix's mentor at Meridian, Marguerite, senses her divided loyalty and offers her a promotion contingent on closing Harrow fast. Beatrix looks at the life she built and finds it measures nothing. Emotional beat: ambition revealed as armor.

chapters.title: The Intercepted Years
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Ulyana reads years of Beatrix's letters and understands the girl she loved never stopped writing. She drives to the mainland, unannounced, and stands in Beatrix's vineyard doorway. Emotional beat: forgiveness arriving ahead of words.

chapters.title: One Night, No Promises
chapters.summary: Both POVs braided. They spend one night without negotiating anything — no futures, no terms, just each other. At dawn, reality returns: Meridian's deadline, the season's last ferry, the vote at the town hall. Emotional beat: borrowed happiness, fully known to be borrowed.

chapters.title: Leaked
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Marguerite discovers Beatrix leaked the marina plans to Ulyana and gives her an ultimatum: recant publicly or be fired and sued. Beatrix asks for twenty-four hours. Emotional beat: the bill for survival finally presented.

chapters.title: Town Hall
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. The island votes on whether to accept Meridian's final offer. Ulyana speaks — not against selling, but for owning their own route through a cooperative, using Beatrix's leaked documents as leverage. The room turns. Emotional beat: courage contagious.

chapters.title: Resignation Letter
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Beatrix walks into Marguerite's office, resigns, and hands over evidence of Meridian's fraudulent survey data — burning the career that saved the vineyard. She leaves with nothing but the letter and her name. Emotional beat: liberation disguised as ruin.

chapters.title: The Last Ferry of the Season
chapters.summary: Both POVs converging. Storm delays; the final crossing looms. Beatrix runs the length of the pier as Ulyana holds the boat past schedule, defying the harbormaster. Beatrix boards with one suitcase. Emotional beat: the climax — a choice made at full speed.

chapters.title: What Survives Winter
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Weeks later: the cooperative's first winter schedule, the vineyard leased to a young couple, two women learning each other again without secrets. Not easy — but honest. Emotional beat: quiet, earned hope.

chapters.title: Ulyana and the Tide
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV, coda. On the spring equinox, Beatrix mails a reply to an eleven-year-old letter, then drops it in the sea from the ferry deck — some answers belong to the tide. She takes the wheel beside Ulyana. Emotional beat: peace as an ongoing practice, not a destination.
